To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the enrichment factors of uranium and other trace elements in soils near breccias pipe uranium mines in northern Arizona, USA are up to 75 and that these enrichment values can be calculated with the use of classical principal component analysis.

1) the EF calculation is a useful metric for assessing the degree of enrichment in a given sample relative to background, but it is important to select an appropriate background and reference element for the calculation; 2) PCA can be used to identify the best element(s) for calculating EF, as well as to identify background compositions and samples with enriched or anthropogenic material; 3) PCA can be applied to any dataset of elemental composition, and the results are useful even when no enrichment of interest
the enrichment factor is a widely used but problematic metric for determining how anthropogenic activity has altered the composition of a sampling media.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new tools to better understand how anthropogenic materials are dispersed in the environment.
the development of new methods for the assessment of anthropogenic and natural enrichment factors in environmental geochemistry.
the development of methods for the assessment and visualization of enrichment of trace elements in soils.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PCA and biplots approach is superior to the EF approach for determining whether a given element is enriched in a sampling medium.
PCA is a powerful tool for understanding the complex geochemical patterns of trace elements in soils, and the biplot is an excellent visual aid for the analyst.
PCA is a valuable and under-utilized tool for identifying elements and/or samples that are enriched in anthropogenic materials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PCA method is a valuable tool for selecting the best background compositions, reference elements, and samples for calculating EF values.
EFs are best used to quantify enrichment, but the biplot approach provides an additional, more holistic perspective on the geochemistry of a dataset.
the PCA and EF are complementary methods for assessing enrichment.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the EF is a powerful metric that can provide useful insight into the presence of anthropogenic materials, but it is important to carefully consider how the EF is calculated and how it should be interpreted.
the EF can be improved when the background composition and reference element are selected based upon the PCA and biplots.
PCA and biplots are useful tools for understanding the distribution of elemental data and for selecting background compositions and reference element(s) for calculating enrichment factors.
